reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Seongsu-dong #Colorless

“A delicious balance of aged sashimi and cooking”

I made a reservation to meet in Seongsu-dong after a long time.
I was intrigued by this place because it appeared on Master of Life and serves raw fish with the interesting concept of fish.

An interior that is too dark may be perfect for couples, but at a drinking party for older people, your eyes get blurry and you can't even see the menu. Haha.
The menu consists of sashimi, sushi, yakimono, agemono, namemono, gohanmono, and menryori.
One Chef (black) handles the living things and the sous chef (white) handles fire.
All the dishes in this house are completed through the collaboration of the two.

I carefully looked through the menu and ordered the menu.
- Sashimi moriawase (assorted sashimi)
- Nodoguro Shioyaki (grilled goldfish)
- Sababo-zushi (mackerel stick sushi)
- Shitake Ebiagedashi (fried shiitake shrimp and dashi sauce)
- Awabi Somen (somen with abalone intestines)
- Service: Burikara Shioyaki (salt-grilled yellowtail gills)

#Otoshi
They served several types of fish with a simple seasoning of tsuyu, green onion, and sesame seeds, and it was more delicious than I expected.
The harmony of fish is especially impressive.
I feel good from the start

#Sashimimoriawase
Sashimi is very good.
It's good that there is no fishy smell at all, but the proper ripening and umami are preserved in each seafood, making me keep coming back for more.
It's also nice that they let you eat it with two versions: salt and soy sauce.

All of the fish in this house is dry-aged, and as if to show off, the fish are hung in a row in the dry-aging cellar.
It's enough to attract attention.
Instead, when you actually eat it, it is hard to tell whether it is regular ripened or dry aged.
I may be new to this, but I don't think there are many people who can tell this apart.
It is a taste that gives the impression that the way the fish is handled, cleaned, and processed is very clean rather than the way it is aged.
I had the best sashimi.

#Grilled Geumtae
It is said that the grilled Geumtae was also dry-aged.
I don't know if it's because of that or if it's small by nature, but the Geumtae you gave me is quite small.
Nevertheless, I don't know if the roast has the feel of dry aging, but it is somewhat dry and has a chewy feel, which makes it different from the regular greasy and soft Geumtae grill.
The grilled Geumtae was also excellent.

#mackerel stick sushi
Compared to the excellent sashimi and grilled gold tae, the mackerel stick sushi is disappointing.
There is no way the fat in the mackerel will be activated if you stamp the pre-made sushi with heated lime.
The rice was cold and hard, so I ate one and didn't eat any more, which was a failure.

#Fried Shiitake Mushroom Shrimp
A Japanese dish where shrimp balls are stuffed with shiitake mushrooms, fried, and served with dashi sauce.
This is so amazing.
The fried food is delicious, but the taste and seasoning of the dashi is perfect.
The perfect garnish to highlight the oroshi and fried green onions you provided.

#Abalone Somen
This too is amazing.
The rich and creamy sauce is good and the somen has a good texture, but the abalone is also cooked amazingly and has the perfect texture.
You're really good at cooking.

#consideration
They prepare the food in advance so that you can enjoy it very deliciously.
Seasonings, toppings, and garnishes such as oroshi, shichimi, and green onions are provided appropriately, and salt, wasabi, and ponzu are also appropriate.

It's a place that does really good food, and it's true that they also do really good fish.
A place recognized for its taste.

Instead, what is disappointing is the customer service.
It was quite busy with just two people ordering food.
Therefore, it should be considered almost impossible to explain food, have conversations, or serve customers.
Perfect for couples who don't want to be disturbed.
For gourmets who enjoy food and taste, it feels like a food factory.
As a result, there is no detailed tiki-taka that you can experience at higher-end Japanese restaurants.

It's definitely delicious.
But I'm not really attracted to it.
It's perfect for these situations: meetings, dates, entertainment, etc.
I'll have to use it for that purpose next time.

Iroh, an izakaya with a great atmosphere in Seongsu-dong!
This place boasts a cozy atmosphere with warm lighting and wood-toned interiors, and you can enjoy delicious food in an emotional space.
I like assorted sashimi. I ordered white cream shrimp as a side dish.
🍣 The assorted sashimi was made with fresh ingredients, and with its large size and clean plating, it was a feast for the eyes and mouth!
🍤 White Cream Shrimp is crispy fried and chewy shrimp that tastes even fresher with sweet and soft white cream sauce and cabbage salad.
It's an izakaya with a perfect atmosphere, recommended for solo drinking, dates, and gatherings!
Emotional interior and warm lighting 💡 I recommend Iro, where you can enjoy the sensibility of Seongsu-dong from a window seat.

reviews.author: Johi
reviews.text:
A satisfying izakaya for the first time in a while

The place is a little small, but the spacing between tables is not too narrow.

Marbled Sesame Nabe not only has a nutty sesame taste, but it also has a spicy taste, so you can eat it without getting tired of it.
I added noodles in the middle, but that's a bit unsatisfactory. I think it would be better to add it together so that the noodles are cooked properly and the soup is soaked properly.

The sashimi is on the good side among regular izakayas. The parts are fresh and the variety is quite diverse.
It was a shame that the ice was so cold that the shrimp shrank a little too much. Still delicious

What was surprisingly delicious was the black sesame karaage. It has a subtle taste of dried fish, but is not too spicy and has a nice nutty taste.

It's a bit pricey, but I don't think it's that expensive for an izakaya.

The staff is very friendly, so it's a place where you can enjoy a meal and a drink together.

Willing to visit again

reviews.author: K
reviews.text: Sponsored // This time, I am leaving an honest review after trying the combo katsu and perilla oil makguksu at Katsugon. Although I always like pork cutlet, I never thought I would have such a satisfying meal in Seongsu-dong. First of all, the best thing about the combo katsu was that it had sirloin, tenderloin, scallops, and shrimp on one plate, so you could enjoy a variety of flavors at once. The sirloin was savory and light, so I was very satisfied from the first bite, and the soft melting texture of the tenderloin was especially impressive. The scallops had a subtle scent of the sea, and the shrimp had a nice chewy texture, so I kept reaching for them.  The perilla oil makguksu we ate together had a lot of seaweed, green onions, and sesame seeds, so it was fragrant, and the noodles were firm, so they naturally balanced out the greasiness of the pork cutlet, making it a really good match. Personally, I felt that this combination was a must-eat set at Katsugon. The atmosphere of the store was warm and comfortable as it was wood-toned, and the staff were friendly, so I was able to stay comfortably throughout the meal. I would like to confidently say that if you are looking for pork cutlet in Seongsu-dong, you will be satisfied even if you visit at least once.

*Japanese fried food franchise

This is a restaurant that catches your eye with bowls filled with fried food.

The Seongsu branch is located on the first floor of a typical two-story house. The front of the store is also very well decorated with a sense of sensibility. I don't know how it is usually, but there is a waiting line before opening, but it is not full, so I was able to eat without waiting.

Underneath the fries are onsen tamago and rice with soy sauce sprinkled on top.
Fried kkwi peppers, which are on every menu, help with the greasiness.

The taste of onsen soba is the same as buckwheat soba, but it is not special. Even though I ate Onsen Tendon and buckwheat soba alone, I was reasonably full, so the amount may be a bit insufficient for an adult male. However, it cannot be denied that the fried food itself is delicious.

reviews.author: Henry Won
reviews.text:
This restaurant is located between old, undeveloped industrial buildings.  It's a bit of a creepy alley during dinner time, but the front of the restaurant is neatly laid out, so you can be sure you've come to the right place.
The interior is one large hall, but it has been designed well to avoid making loud noises.  There is soft music playing and the spacing between tables is wide, so it's great for conversation without being disturbed while eating.
I ordered salmon avocado tartare, fish roe oil pasta, kaisendon, unagi-don, and futomaki, and for alcohol, I ordered spring (shiso).  The food not only looks nice, it tastes good too.  In particular, the fish roe oil pasta has the noodles cooked just right and the sauce has a good balance of oiliness and lightness.
My group misunderstood that the uni (sea urchin) in the menu picture for pasta and tartare was optional, so they added extra uni (KRW 20,000) to each dish. However, looking at the menu, the pasta and tartare included uni by default, and the additional uni (sea urchin) in the menu picture was double the original amount on a separate plate.  The uni was of good quality and I enjoyed all the extra uni so I didn't feel like my money was wasted.
However, when ordering the restaurant's signature drink, Spring, Summer, Autumn and Autumn, the person taking the order did not know that there were four types of alcohol (spring, summer, fall, and winter), so he asked another experienced server and came back.  The skill level of the server taking orders was disappointing.  When my group ordered two extra uni, I sometimes think that if they had been there to guide us about ordering, we might not have had the pleasure of eating a lot of uni.  The service itself was flawless and smooth.

reviews.author: S Y
reviews.text:
The store is on the second floor, and the entrance is in an alley, so I was able to find Suage by looking at the sign at the entrance to the alley.

It's an unfamiliar food, but it's a little easier to see because there's a picture.

The order form is unique; you can write up to four items per page, and one space is used for each order menu. I chose the basic level 3 spiciness and the rice was normal. If you choose more, 1,000 won will be added.

There are instructions on how to compose the menu, but I ordered the already prepared menu. Pickled radish is served as a basic side dish.

The chicken skewer curry (13,500 won) I ordered was blacker than expected and had a nice smell. I feel like it will be delicious. The rice was spread thinly so there wasn't a lot of it.

I tried a bite of the soup, and it felt similar to the first time I ate pupatppong curry. Familiar yet unfamiliar flavors that are so well balanced! It's a taste that most Koreans will like. Of course, this is just my opinion, but I feel like there will be no likes or dislikes.

It contained two chicken skewers, half a boiled egg, sweet pumpkin, oyster mushrooms, carrots, eggplant, and sweet potatoes. It had a good texture, probably because it was cooked well over a fire before being added to the soup.

Each skewer wasn't that big, so the quantity was small, but it was okay because the chicken skewers were sturdy.

For someone who is not good at eating spicy food, the soup curry spiciness level 3 was moderately spicy, and if you like spicy food, I think you can eat up to level 4 without any problems.

The inside of the store is clean and the atmosphere is nice. The speed at which the food came out was not slow, so the turnaround of seats was quick.

The amount was small by my standards, but it was okay because I was full after eating all the soup. Seongsu is a little far away, so I'll have to go to another nearby branch next time. The curry soup is delicious. Recommended.

reviews.author: Soyo Kim
reviews.text:
I finally found a decent restaurant in Seongsu-dong.
Anyway, even considering that Seongsu-dong costs more than 10,000 won, I was always disappointed that I couldn't get my money's worth, but it is a restaurant that satisfies the uniqueness, taste, atmosphere, and number of tables.

There was only one table for two, so it seemed a bit odd that people were eating alone.
It was okay because there were about 10 tables for 4 people. There are a lot of people, but I think that's why there isn't much waiting.

I ordered fried chicken leg soup, and I'm sure some people found it greasy because the vegetables and chicken were fried or grilled. Other than that part being disappointing, it was delicious.

Vegetables in particular, broccoli was the best, and I always liked lotus root, so it would be difficult to evaluate it objectively. I recommend this part if you have a favorite vegetable.

While waiting for the soup, I looked around and saw that everyone was leaving rice. I didn't know why, but I found out after eating it. reviews.text:
I had Omakase lunch with a friend at Sushi Omoto located in Seongsu-dong, Seoul. It was a small and calm space, and I was able to leisurely enjoy the neatly prepared course. The staff was very friendly, so I was able to enjoy the entire meal comfortably, and the explanations were concise and easy to understand.

The course was a potato puree chawanmushi that slightly opened up the palate, followed by fresh fish such as flounder, sea bream, herring, red meat tuna, horse mackerel, and belly fat. The texture of each ingredient was clearly felt, and the well-balanced harmony with the Shari was also impressive.

Afterwards, ingredients with distinct textures such as squid, shrimp, and monkfish liver appeared at appropriate times to create a sense of rhythm, and the warm and deep flavor of Goto udon gently wrapped around the inside. Lastly, it was finished off with sea eel, futomaki, gyoku, and refreshing sorbet.

The overall composition and tempo were stable, and it was a satisfying meal thanks to the care put into each and every detail.

The inside of the store has a clean, regular restaurant atmosphere, but there is a slightly exotic atmosphere in the tables and small decorations. Yukyukmyeongwan has a unique table with mahjong paddles under the glass, adding to the exotic atmosphere.

reviews.author: Ga young Bae
reviews.text: Because I had a hangover the day before, I couldn't get rid of ramen even after eating it, so I went to eat jjamppong. There are about ten tables, but it is said that people wait in line to eat here during weekday lunches, probably because it is a neighborhood with a lot of office workers. Since Jjamppong is the main dish, there are many types of Jjamppong. However, the jjamppong rice did not have any other toppings such as chadol jjamppong rice or oyster jjamppong rice, and there was only regular jjamppong rice. They said there was a lot of jjamppong here, so two people ordered one chadol jjamppong and a mini sweet and sour pork. Perhaps because it was a busy time, the menu came out a little over 5 minutes after ordering. First of all, the broth of the chadol jjamppong was thick like beef bone broth, perhaps because of the chadol in it, so it was good for hangovers. The whole garlic was chewy, but there was also a lot of garlic and onion in it. I don't really like the texture of noodles that taste like flour, but I was very satisfied with the texture as it was somewhere between flour and chewy noodles. The mini sweet and sour pork was thinly fried and had a good texture and taste. I left after a good hangover.

reviews.author: Sean Choi

reviews.text: [This is a review written after receiving and experiencing the service] This is a premium Chinese restaurant that I visited while having a lunch date in Seoul Forest. reviews.author: Mungrini
reviews.text: It seems to be a good place for family gatherings or group gatherings as it has a group room. On the day I visited, all the rooms were full due to first birthday parties and group gatherings. These days, there are many places where Jjajangmyeon is bland and tasteless, but China Plain Jjajangmyeon is the Matdori Jjajangmyeon with a strong Chunjang flavor that I enjoyed eating when I was young. I'm so glad I found a Chinese restaurant in Seongsu. I was very satisfied with the amount of food and the quality of seafood and meat. The dumplings are especially delicious, probably because they are handmade at the store. The meat dumplings were the best!

reviews.author: Flipply

Just by looking at the photo, you can tell that the ingredients are fresh, good, and large. It was the most satisfying Chinese course meal I've ever had.
If you are looking for a clean and stylish Chinese restaurant, go there!

This is a place where chefs from luxury hotels lead the cooking.
This is a restaurant where you can trust that whatever you order will be delicious.

reviews.text: This is a place where I have a truly satisfying experience every time I go. I have never been disappointed with either the individual menu or the course menu. reviews.author: Soyeon Park
reviews.text: It's a high-end Chinese restaurant in the basement of Galleria Foret in Seoul Forest, but the prices aren't that expensive. The atmosphere is luxurious! The butter sweet and sour pork topped with chives was delicious, but the chive jjajangmyeon was the best. It seems like there is a lot of experimentation with food here. I think the chefs have a lot of unique food. Next time, I have to go eat Korean beef black bean noodles. The Korean beef jjajangmyeon reminds me of the movie Parasite. As soon as it opens at 12 o'clock, people with reservations come in all at once and it is immediately full.
I thought it would be too tight since the usage time is limited to 80 minutes, but the food came out quickly and the portions were not large, so I had enough time.
Unfortunately, I couldn't try the Dongpo Pork because it wasn't available for order. I ordered Balsamic Kwavaro, but the combination of balsamic sauce, olives, and strawberries was quite refreshing, and when you dip it in Tzuran, it transforms into a completely different taste. What's the magic? It was a fun experience
Bologna tofu + cream risotto was also a moderately spicy fusion. The combination of mapo tofu and cream risotto was quite good.
I've always been curious about Chef Choi Hyun-seok's cooking, and this is how I tried it haha. It was a restaurant that left a lot of lingering memories.

reviews.author: Kim Dong-yoon
reviews.text:
Visited on 26.01.22. A restaurant run by chef Choi Hyun-seok. I made a reservation in advance through Catch Table and visited. The restaurant concept is a fusion of Chinese and Italian, and each dish served was unique. And the food seems to have a darker Western flavor than Chinese food.

What I was most looking forward to was, of course, the mapo lamb ribs. I appeared on Black and White Chef and was eliminated with this dish. There are some differences between what you see on TV and the actual food. But it was the most delicious food I ate that day.

The second fried spring roll was delicious. It had whole basil and shrimp inside, so I wanted to order it again.

Vongole pasta is just pasta made with Jjamppong noodles. There doesn't seem to be anything special about it.

The balsamic curry comes with tsuran, and it is definitely more delicious to eat with tsuran than to eat it on its own.
